ESP32-C5 brings dual-band Wi-Fi 6 to hobbyists

Espressif has started shipping the ESP32-C5, the first chip in its lineup that supports both the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands. For home automation projects this means less interference in crowded apartment buildings, where the 2.4 GHz band is often saturated by neighbours' routers.

The chip pairs a RISC-V core running at 240 MHz with 384 KB of SRAM. It also supports Bluetooth LE 5 and IEEE 802.15.4, so a single board can act as a Thread border router or a Zigbee coordinator while staying on Wi-Fi.

Development boards are available for around ten dollars, and the ESP-IDF framework already includes examples for the new radio features. Arduino support is expected later this year, which should make the chip popular in DIY circles.
